issues.legal_issue: A mortgage of an entire proprietary share includes the proprietary interest in sir land pertaining to that share even when the sir land is not expressly described.
material_facts: The mortgagor executed a simple mortgage without possession of his entire relevant share in the village.
The deed described the share and rights and privileges pertaining to the village but did not expressly mention sir land or exclude it.
The mortgagees later obtained a sale decree and a sale certificate conveying the share with all rights pertaining to it.
issues.conclusion: The mortgage included the mortgagor’s proprietary rights in the sir land pertaining to the mortgaged share, and the sale certificate conveyed those rights to the mortgagees.
issues.legal_principle: The mortgage covered all proprietary rights in the share unless sir land was specifically excluded. Sections 68 and 69 of the Central Provinces Land Revenue Act, 1917, distinguish sir land from khudkashat land. Sections 49 and 50 of the Central Provinces Tenancy Act, 1920, apply when a proprietor loses the right to occupy sir land; a mortgage without possession does not cause that loss, so no reservation or sanction under section 50 was required. The words conveying all rights pertaining to the share included the proprietary interest in sir land.

rule.if: mortgage_of_proprietary_share and entire_proprietary_share_mortgaged and sir_land_not_expressly_excluded and mortgage_without_possession

predicates.mortgage_of_proprietary_share: The transaction involved a mortgage of a proprietary share.
predicates.entire_proprietary_share_mortgaged: The mortgagor mortgaged the whole of the relevant proprietary share.
predicates.sir_land_not_expressly_excluded: The mortgage instrument did not expressly exclude the sir land pertaining to the share.
predicates.mortgage_without_possession: The mortgage did not transfer possession from the mortgagor.

issues.definition: When a whole proprietary share is mortgaged without possession and its sir land is not expressly excluded, the proprietary rights in that sir land are included in the mortgage.

issues.legal_issue: Land formerly held under an ex-proprietary tenancy becomes an accession to a subsisting mortgage when that tenancy ends and the land comes into the possession of the proprietor’s successor in management.
material_facts: The mortgaged share included the proprietary rights in the sir land.
After the appellant purchased the mortgagor’s share subject to the mortgage, the mortgagor became an ex-proprietary tenant of the sir land.
The ex-proprietary tenancy was later extinguished while the mortgage remained subsisting, and the land came into the appellant’s possession as lambardar.
issues.conclusion: The land became an accession to the mortgaged property under section 70 of the Transfer of Property Act, and the mortgagees were entitled to a share in it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 70 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, applies when property becomes an accession to mortgaged property while the mortgage subsists. When the ex-proprietary tenancy ended, the land came into the possession of the lambardar for the proprietary body and became khudkashat; because the mortgage already covered the proprietary rights in the land, it was an accession to the mortgage. The Court found no illegality in the accession.

rule.if: mortgage_accession_claim and mortgage_covers_underlying_proprietary_interest and mortgage_still_subsisting and ex_proprietary_tenancy_ends and land_enters_proprietor_representative_possession

predicates.mortgage_accession_claim: The proceeding concerns a mortgagee’s claim to property said to have accrued to mortgaged property.
predicates.mortgage_covers_underlying_proprietary_i: The mortgage covers the proprietary interest in the land that later comes into possession.
predicates.mortgage_still_subsisting: The mortgage remains in force when the land comes into possession.
predicates.ex_proprietary_tenancy_ends: The former proprietor’s ex-proprietary tenancy in the land is extinguished.
predicates.land_enters_proprietor_representative_po: After the tenancy ends, the land comes into the possession of a person managing it for the proprietary body.

issues.definition: If a mortgage covering the land’s proprietary interest remains in force when an ex-proprietary tenancy ends and the land enters the representative’s possession, the land is an accession in which the mortgagee is entitled to a share.

issues.legal_issue: A claim to a share in land held for the proprietary body is not barred merely because the land was not specified in an earlier mortgage suit seeking sale of the mortgaged share.
material_facts: Certain lands were nominally recorded in the mortgagor’s mother’s name but were actually in the mortgagor’s possession.
After the appellant acquired the mortgagor’s share, the appellant came into possession of those lands as lambardar and held them for the entire body of proprietors.
The earlier mortgage suit sought sale of the mortgaged share, and the lands were not specified in its plaint.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were entitled to a share in the lands, and their claim was not barred by Order II, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure merely because the lands had not been specified in the earlier mortgage suit.
issues.legal_principle: In a suit for sale of a mortgaged share, it is not necessary to specify every land in the mortgagor’s possession; the lands pertaining to the share pass with it on sale. The Court distinguished Hazarilal v. Hazarimal, A.I.R. 1923 Nag. 130, and Seth Manakchand v. Chaube Manohar Lal, A.I.R. 1944 P.C. 46, as cases concerning foreclosure, whereas the earlier suit here sought sale of the share. Order II, rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure therefore did not bar the later claim.

predicates.later_share_claim_after_mortgage_sale: The claimant brings a later claim for a share in land after an earlier mortgage sale.
predicates.earlier_suit_sought_sale_of_mortgaged_sh: The earlier mortgage suit sought sale of the mortgaged share rather than foreclosure.
predicates.lands_omitted_from_earlier_plaint: The lands claimed later were not specified in the earlier suit’s plaint.
predicates.lambardar_holds_lands_for_proprietary_bo: The lambardar possesses the lands on behalf of the entire proprietary body.

issues.definition: When a later share claim concerns omitted lands held by the lambardar for the proprietary body, and the earlier mortgage suit sought sale of the mortgaged share, the omission does not bar the claim and the claimant is entitled to a share.

issues.legal_issue: A mortgagee is entitled to a share in lands that come into a lambardar’s possession through ordinary management, subject to payment of the mortgagee’s proportionate share of the expenses incurred in obtaining them.
material_facts: While managing the village as lambardar, the appellant came into possession of certain other lands through surrender or other ordinary management processes.
The appellant incurred expenses in suits through which some of those lands came into his possession.
The High Court allowed the respondents a share subject to payment of proportionate expenses.
issues.conclusion: The respondents were entitled to a share in those lands upon payment of their proportionate share of the expenses incurred by the appellant.
issues.legal_principle: The Court upheld the High Court’s determination that the mortgagees were entitled to a share in lands acquired by the lambardar in the ordinary course of management, subject to contribution toward proportionate expenses incurred in the relevant suits.

predicates.claim_to_lands_acquired_in_ordinary_mana: The claimant seeks a share in lands obtained through ordinary management of the property.
predicates.lambardar_obtained_possession_for_propri: The lambardar obtained possession of the lands while managing them for the proprietary body.
predicates.expenses_incurred_to_obtain_lands: Expenses were incurred in proceedings through which the lands came into possession.

issues.definition: When lands are obtained by a lambardar for the proprietary body through ordinary management and expenses were incurred to obtain them, the claimant receives a share subject to proportionate expenses.
